overview: This file traces U.S. Department of State efforts from 1930 to 1934 to obtain and transmit telephone—and, in 1931, telegraph—statistics for Japanese-administered communications systems in the Kwantung Leased Territory and elsewhere in Manchuria, chiefly for the American Telephone and Telegraph Company. It contains State Department instructions, consular despatches from Dairen, statistical questionnaires comparing conditions in 1929–1931, and cross-reference sheets pointing to later correspondence. The documents record exchanges, telephones, wire mileage, employees, traffic, revenues, investment, population, and city-level development, while repeatedly noting that changing territorial coverage and the unavailability of South Manchuria Railway Zone data complicated comparisons.

people.name: Thomas
people.role: Author of the referenced 1932 despatch from Dairen; full name and position are not stated on the cross-reference sheet

people.name: John Carter Vincent
people.role: U.S. consular officer identified on the 1934 cross-reference sheet only by surname

subfiles.title: Instruction requesting updated Kwantung telephone statistics
subfiles.about: The Department of State requests updated government and private telephone statistics for the Kwantung Leased Territory on behalf of the American Telephone and Telegraph Company.
subfiles.summary: The instruction refers to an earlier request of July 23, 1929, and encloses forms for updating the previous year's information to January 1, 1930. It also supplies the consulate with the company's publication, Telephone and Telegraph Statistics of the World, and asks that the completed statistics be returned in triplicate under a covering despatch.

subfiles.title: Despatch from Coville transmitting 1930 telephone statistics
subfiles.from: Cabot Coville, American Vice Consul at Dairen
subfiles.about: Coville submits the completed telephone questionnaire and explains that its territorial coverage excludes the South Manchuria Railway Zone.
subfiles.summary: Coville transmits the questionnaire requested by the American Telephone and Telegraph Company. He cautions that the 1929 consular report covered both the Kwantung Leased Territory and the South Manchuria Railway Zone, whereas the new figures cover only the leased territory. The Kwantung Government's Bureau of Communications had orally informed the consulate that it would not make the railway-zone statistics available that year.

subfiles.title: Kwantung telephone statistics for 1929–1930
subfiles.from: Bureau of Communications, Kwantung Government, transmitted by the American Consulate at Dairen
subfiles.to: U.S. Department of State and American Telephone and Telegraph Company
subfiles.about: The enclosure tabulates Japanese government telephone operations and city-level telephone development in the Kwantung Leased Territory.
subfiles.summary: The principal table compares March 31, 1929 and March 31, 1930 figures for central offices, manual and automatic telephones, wire length, employment, calls, revenue, and population. It records growth from 9,580 to 10,732 telephones and from about 83.3 million to 96.1 million annual conversations. A second table gives population and limited telephone figures for Dairen, Port Arthur, Chinchon, Pulantion, and Pitsuwo.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to AT&T acknowledgment
subfiles.about: The sheet refers researchers to a letter acknowledging receipt of the telephone statistics sent from Dairen.
subfiles.summary: The filing note directs readers to file 893.75/83 for an October 29, 1930 letter from the American Telephone and Telegraph Company. According to the note, the company expressed appreciation for the Dairen statistics transmitted by the Department.

subfiles.title: Langdon despatch transmitting the 1931 communications survey
subfiles.from: William R. Langdon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.about: Langdon submits a survey of telephone conditions in the Kwantung Leased Territory for transmission to the American Telephone and Telegraph Company.
subfiles.summary: Acting under the Department's instruction of June 4, 1931, Langdon encloses three copies of the requested survey. The survey responds to the American Telephone and Telegraph Company's request of May 23, 1931.

subfiles.title: Kwantung telephone and telegraph statistics for 1930–1931
subfiles.from: American Consulate at Dairen using Japanese government statistics
subfiles.to: U.S. Department of State and American Telephone and Telegraph Company
subfiles.about: The enclosure compares telephone development in 1930 and 1931 and supplies a separate statistical profile of the Japanese government telegraph system.
subfiles.summary: The telephone table reports growth from 10,732 to 11,470 instruments, from roughly 96.1 million to 106 million annual conversations, and from ¥1.17 million to ¥1.51 million in revenue. A city table provides population and telephone figures for Dairen, Port Arthur, Chinchou, Pulantien, and Pitzuwo, while flagging a possible inconsistency in the earlier Dairen total. The telegraph table reports 87 offices, more than 3.17 million messages, ¥874,632 in revenue, ¥4.28 million in investment, and 91 employees for March 31, 1931.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Thomas despatch on Kwantung statistics
subfiles.about: The sheet points to a separate despatch concerning telephone statistics for the Kwantung Leased Territory.
subfiles.summary: The filing note directs researchers to file 893.75/121 for despatch no. 18 from Dairen, dated August 30, 1932. The referenced despatch is described only as concerning telephone statistics of the Kwantung Leased Territory.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Vincent despatch on Manchurian statistical coverage
subfiles.about: The sheet points to a despatch explaining the geographic coverage of telephone statistics for the Mukden and Harbin districts.
subfiles.summary: The filing note refers to file 893.75/149 for despatch no. 77 from Dairen, dated April 11, 1934. It states that the Mukden and Harbin district statistics cover communications throughout Manchuria except those in the South Manchuria Railway area and its towns and in the Kwantung Leased Territory.

interest: The file provides unusually detailed quantitative evidence for the expansion of Japanese-administered telephone and telegraph infrastructure in colonial Manchuria, including traffic, staffing, revenues, investment, and urban distribution. It is especially useful because the consular correspondence documents changes in statistical boundaries and explicit refusals to release South Manchuria Railway Zone data, warning historians against treating successive totals as directly comparable. The city tables and their flagged inconsistencies also reveal how American officials and AT&T evaluated the reliability of overseas communications statistics.
